hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes training into divergence, as in the large drops in experiments 17 and 3.
A very small learning rate undertrains in 243 epochs, so a larger step helps.
Lowering a too-high learning rate restores stable training, as in experiments 12, 18 and 52.
Wider networks with a high learning rate have larger effective updates and are more likely to diverge, as in experiment 97.
Deeper networks are less stable at high learning rates, so adding a layer hurts more there.
A larger batch means fewer updates, and with a tiny learning rate this makes undertraining worse, as in experiment 21.
A strong L2 penalty already underfits, and raising it further hurts.
A wide network is already high-capacity and harder to optimize, so extra depth adds instability rather than benefit.
Wide layers need smaller learning rates, so raising it overshoots, as in experiments 3, 11 and 15.
With a very large batch there are too few updates, so a smaller batch gives more steps and better fit.
